props.doc:
Email: notification on one side, phishing response on the other.

Send Email is deliberately its own connector rather than a hidden platform
capability, because it is a command like any other - it has a credential, a
schema, a risk level, an egress allowlist and an audit record. A platform
that can mail anyone from anywhere without appearing in the command
catalogue is a platform with an unlogged exfiltration path.

def param(kind, **extra):
    """One input property, in JSON Schema terms."""
    spec = {"type": kind} if kind not in ("ipv4", "hostname") else {"type": "string"}
    spec.update(extra)
    return spec


def cmd(key, name, method, url, inputs, outputs, extract=None, risk="low",
        effect="read", doc="", techniques=None, undo=None, timeout_ms=30000,
        required=None, category="integration", body=None, success=None):
    """
    One command definition.

    Structured JSON in, structured JSON out. The output_schema is what the
    playbook validator type-checks the next step against, so a command whose
    schema lies fails at publish rather than at 03:00.
    """
    definition = {
        "key": key,
        "name": name,
        "category": category,
        "kind": "http",
        "input_schema": {
            "type": "object",
            "required": list(inputs.keys()) if required is None else required,
            "properties": inputs,
            "additionalProperties": False,
        },
        "output_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": outputs},
        "implementation": {
            "method": method,
            "url": url,
            "extract": extract or {},
            "success_codes": success or [200, 201, 202, 204],
        },
        "required_permissions": ["commands.execute"],
        "required_capabilities": ["net"],
        "timeout_ms": timeout_ms,
        "risk_level": risk,
        "effect": effect,
        "trust_level": "trusted",
        "technique_ids": techniques or [],
        "doc": doc,
    }
    if body is not None:
        definition["implementation"]["body"] = body
    if effect == "mutating":
        # A mutating command with no dry-run example would make dry run a lie,
        # and the registry validator refuses it.
        definition["dry_run_example"] = {"dry_run": True, "would_call": key}
    if undo:
        # Named, not inferred. The platform never invents a rollback.
        definition["undo_command"] = undo
    if risk == "high":
        definition["required_permissions"] = ["commands.execute", _permission_for(key)]
    return definition


def _permission_for(key):
    """High-risk commands need the response permission that matches them."""
    action = key.split(".", 1)[1]
    if "isolate" in action or "contain" in action or "quarantine_host" in action:
        return "response.isolate"
    if "block" in action:
        return "response.block"
    if "disable" in action or "suspend" in action:
        return "response.disable_account"
    if "revoke" in action or "signout" in action:
        return "response.revoke_sessions"
    if "delete" in action or "purge" in action or "remove_mail" in action:
        return "response.delete_mail"
    if "firewall" in action or "policy" in action:
        return "response.firewall"
    return "response.isolate"


def field(name, label, kind="text", required=True, default=None,
          options=None, help="", placeholder=""):
    # One thing an operator must be told before this tool can be reached.
    return {
        "name": name, "label": label, "kind": kind, "required": required,
        "default": default, "options": options or [], "help": help,
        "placeholder": placeholder,
    }


def connector(cid, name, vendor, category, auth, base_url, allowlist, commands,
              min_permissions=None, rate_limit=None, health=None,
              version="1.0.0", setup=None, derive=None, ingest=None,
              hunt=None):
    # A connector manifest. Installing one publishes its commands; no engine
    # change.
    #
    # setup is what THIS vendor needs before it can be reached, and no two
    # agree: CrowdStrike wants a cloud region, Sentinel a tenant and a
    # workspace, Splunk a host and a port. Asking every connector for a
    # client id and a secret asked the two questions they happen to share
    # and none of the ones that make a connection work.
    fields = list(setup or [])

    # Which setting the commands of this connector actually read. Most say
    # base_url; a few front a protocol that is not HTTP and say gateway_url
    # instead, and asking those for a base_url nothing reads is how a form
    # grows a field that does nothing.
    setting = "base_url"
    if "{{" in base_url:
        inner = base_url.split("{{", 1)[1].split("}}", 1)[0].strip()
        setting = inner.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] if inner else "base_url"

    if not any(f["name"] == setting for f in fields):
        # Every connector can at least be pointed elsewhere: a regional
        # cloud, a tenant-specific host, an on-premise appliance.
        # A connector whose base_url is itself a template has no host until
        # someone supplies one, so there is nothing to prefill and the field
        # is the only way the connection can exist at all.
        templated = "{{" in base_url
        fields.insert(0, field(
            setting, "API base URL", kind="url",
            default=None if templated else base_url,
            help="Change for a regional cloud or an on-premise appliance."
                 if not templated else "The hostname this tenant answers on."))

    return {
        "setup": fields,
        # Settings a vendor addresses by a composite of the ones a person
        # can actually be asked for. Nobody knows their workspace ARM id;
        # everybody knows their subscription, resource group and workspace
        # name, and the id is those three in a fixed shape.
        "derive": derive or {},
        # How this product is polled for alerts: which command lists them,
        # which turns ids into objects, and where the timestamp lives that
        # the watermark advances to. A connector without it can still
        # receive a webhook; it just cannot be asked.
        "ingest": ingest or {},
        # Which command runs an arbitrary hunt query, what the query
        # parameter is called, and what language an engineer is writing.
        # A tool without this cannot be hunted in - which is most of them,
        # because a firewall is not a place you go looking.
        "hunt": hunt or {},
        "id": cid, "name": name, "vendor": vendor, "category": category,
        "version": version, "auth": auth, "base_url": base_url,
        "egress_allowlist": allowlist,
        "min_vendor_permissions": min_permissions or [],
        "rate_limit": rate_limit or {},
        "health_check": health or {},
        "commands": commands,
        "publisher": "master-soar",
        "signature": "",
    }


smtp = connector(
    "smtp.generic", "Send Email (SMTP)", "generic", "email",
    {"kind": "basic", "roles": ["username", "password"]},
    "{{ integration.config.gateway_url }}",
    ["{{ integration.config.smtp_host }}"],
    health={"path": "/health"},
    setup=[
        field("gateway_url", "Mail gateway URL", kind="url",
              placeholder="https://mail-gateway.client.example"),
        field("smtp_host", "SMTP host", placeholder="smtp.client.example"),
        field("from_address", "From address",
              placeholder="soc@client.example",
              help="What the recipient sees. Use an address the SPF record of the sending domain allows."),
    ],
    commands=[
        cmd("email.send", "Send Email", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.gateway_url }}/send",
            {"to": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "format": "email"},
                    "minItems": 1, "maxItems": 50},
             "cc": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "format": "email"},
                    "maxItems": 50},
             "subject": param("string", maxLength=200),
             "body": param("string", maxLength=100000),
             "body_type": param("string", enum=["text", "html"]),
             "attachments": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"},
                             "maxItems": 10},
             "importance": param("string", enum=["low", "normal", "high"])},
            {"message_id": {"type": "string"}, "accepted": {"type": "array"}},
            {"message_id": "$.message_id", "accepted": "$.accepted"},
            risk="medium", effect="mutating",
            required=["to", "subject", "body"],
            category="notification",
            body={"to": "{{ inputs.to | json }}", "cc": "{{ inputs.cc | json }}",
                  "subject": "{{ inputs.subject }}",
                  "body": "{{ inputs.body }}",
                  "body_type": "{{ inputs.body_type | default('html') }}",
                  "importance": "{{ inputs.importance | default('normal') }}"},
            doc="Notify an analyst, an asset owner, or an affected user. HTML bodies "
                "are rendered through the html filter, so incident content cannot "
                "inject markup into a message the SOC sends on its own letterhead. "
                "The recipient list is capped: a mistake in a loop should not become "
                "a mail-out to the whole estate."),

        cmd("email.send_templated", "Send Email from Template", "POST",
            "{{ integration.config.gateway_url }}/send-template",
            {"to": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string", "format": "email"},
                    "minItems": 1, "maxItems": 500},
             "template": param("string", pattern="^[a-z0-9_]{3,64}$"),
             "variables": {"type": "object"}},
            {"message_ids": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}},
            risk="medium", effect="mutating", category="notification",
            required=["to", "template"],
            body={"to": "{{ inputs.to | json }}",
                  "template": "{{ inputs.template }}",
                  "variables": "{{ inputs.variables | json }}"},
            doc="Bulk user notification - the 'a phishing message was removed from "
                "your mailbox' case. The template is a name, so the body cannot be "
                "built from attacker-supplied content at all."),
    ],
)

graph_mail = connector(
    "microsoft.exchange_online", "Microsoft 365 Mail", "Microsoft", "email",
    {"kind": "oauth2_client", "roles": ["client_id", "client_secret"],
     "token_url": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/{{ integration.config.tenant_id }}/oauth2/v2.0/token",
     "scope": "https://graph.microsoft.com/.default"},
    "https://graph.microsoft.com",
    ["graph.microsoft.com", "login.microsoftonline.com",
     "security.microsoft.com"],
    min_permissions=["Mail.ReadWrite", "Mail.Send",
                     "SecurityEvents.ReadWrite.All", "ThreatHunting.Read.All"],
    health={"path": "/v1.0/organization"},
    setup=[
        field("tenant_id", "Entra tenant id",
              placeholder="00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000",
              help="The directory the tenant lives in. It is part of the token endpoint, so a wrong one fails at sign-in."),
        field("shared_mailbox", "Shared mailbox", required=False,
              placeholder="soc@client.example",
              help="Where a purge or a send runs from when the playbook does not name one."),
    ],
    commands=[
        cmd("m365mail.search_messages", "M365: Search Mailbox", "GET",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/{{ inputs.mailbox | urlencode }}/messages?$search=%22{{ inputs.query | urlencode }}%22&$top={{ inputs.limit | default(25) }}",
            {"mailbox": param("string", format="email"),
             "query": param("string", maxLength=1000),
             "limit": param("integer", maximum=100)},
            {"messages": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}},
             "count": {"type": "integer"}},
            {"messages": "$.value"}, required=["mailbox", "query"]),

        cmd("m365mail.find_recipients", "M365: Find Message Recipients", "POST",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery",
            {"sender": param("string", format="email"),
             "subject": param("string"),
             "days": param("integer", minimum=1, maximum=30)},
            {"recipients": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}},
             "delivered_count": {"type": "integer"}},
            {"recipients": "$.results"}, required=["sender"], timeout_ms=120000,
            body={"Query": "EmailEvents | where SenderFromAddress =~ \"{{ inputs.sender }}\" | where Timestamp > ago({{ inputs.days | default(7) }}d) | project RecipientEmailAddress, DeliveryAction, Subject, NetworkMessageId"},
            doc="Who else got it. The question that turns one reported phish into "
                "the real scope of the incident."),

        cmd("m365mail.get_message", "M365: Get Message", "GET",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/{{ inputs.mailbox | urlencode }}/messages/{{ inputs.message_id | urlencode }}",
            {"mailbox": param("string"), "message_id": param("string")},
            {"subject": {"type": "string"}, "sender": {"type": "string"},
             "received": {"type": "string"}, "body": {"type": "string"},
             "headers": {"type": "array"}},
            {"subject": "$.subject", "sender": "$.sender.emailAddress.address",
             "received": "$.receivedDateTime", "body": "$.body.content",
             "headers": "$.internetMessageHeaders"},
            doc="Full message including headers. Headers are what the phishing "
                "analysis actually needs - SPF, DKIM, the real return path."),

        cmd("m365mail.move_to_junk", "M365: Move Message to Junk", "POST",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/{{ inputs.mailbox | urlencode }}/messages/{{ inputs.message_id | urlencode }}/move",
            {"mailbox": param("string"), "message_id": param("string")},
            {"moved_id": {"type": "string"}}, {"moved_id": "$.id"},
            risk="medium", effect="mutating",
            body={"destinationId": "junkemail"},
            doc="The reversible option. Prefer it to deletion when the verdict is "
                "suspicious rather than confirmed."),

        cmd("m365mail.soft_delete_message", "M365: Soft Delete Message", "DELETE",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/{{ inputs.mailbox | urlencode }}/messages/{{ inputs.message_id | urlencode }}",
            {"mailbox": param("string"), "message_id": param("string")},
            {"deleted": {"type": "boolean"}},
            risk="high", effect="mutating", success=[204],
            doc="Recoverable from Deleted Items. This is the containment command "
                "a phishing playbook should reach for; hard purge is a separate, "
                "deliberately harder-to-reach command."),

        cmd("m365mail.purge_from_all_mailboxes", "M365: Purge From All Mailboxes",
            "POST",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/collaboration/analyzedEmails/remediate",
            {"network_message_ids": {"type": "array",
                                     "items": {"type": "string"},
                                     "minItems": 1, "maxItems": 1000},
             "action": param("string", enum=["softDelete", "hardDelete",
                                             "moveToJunk", "moveToInbox"]),
             "reason": param("string", maxLength=1000)},
            {"remediation_id": {"type": "string"}, "affected": {"type": "integer"}},
            risk="high", effect="mutating", timeout_ms=180000,
            required=["network_message_ids", "action", "reason"],
            body={"networkMessageIds": "{{ inputs.network_message_ids | json }}",
                  "action": "{{ inputs.action }}",
                  "reason": "{{ inputs.reason }}"},
            doc="Tenant-wide removal. HIGH risk and capped at 1000 messages: a "
                "wrong purge is unrecoverable for the recipients and indistinguishable "
                "from an attacker covering their tracks. The reason is mandatory and "
                "goes into the audit record."),

        cmd("m365mail.block_sender", "M365: Block Sender Tenant-Wide", "POST",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/security/tiIndicators",
            {"sender": param("string", format="email"),
             "expires_days": param("integer", minimum=1, maximum=365),
             "description": param("string")},
            {"indicator_id": {"type": "string"}}, {"indicator_id": "$.id"},
            risk="high", effect="mutating", undo="m365mail.unblock_sender",
            required=["sender", "description"],
            body={"action": "block", "emailSenderAddress": "{{ inputs.sender }}",
                  "targetProduct": "Microsoft Defender for Office 365",
                  "description": "{{ inputs.description }}",
                  "expirationDateTime": "{{ inputs.expires_days | default(90) }}"},
            doc="Blocks carry an expiry on purpose. A tenant block list that only "
                "grows becomes an outage nobody can explain two years later."),

        cmd("m365mail.unblock_sender", "M365: Unblock Sender", "DELETE",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/security/tiIndicators/{{ inputs.indicator_id | urlencode }}",
            {"indicator_id": param("string")},
            {"removed": {"type": "boolean"}},
            risk="medium", effect="mutating", success=[204]),

        cmd("m365mail.get_message_trace", "M365: Message Trace", "POST",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/runHuntingQuery",
            {"message_id": param("string"), "days": param("integer", maximum=30)},
            {"events": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            {"events": "$.results"}, required=["message_id"],
            body={"Query": "EmailEvents | where NetworkMessageId == \"{{ inputs.message_id }}\" | join kind=leftouter EmailPostDeliveryEvents on NetworkMessageId"},
            doc="Delivery outcome and anything that happened after delivery - "
                "including whether the user clicked."),

        cmd("m365mail.get_mailbox_rules", "M365: Get Mailbox Rules", "GET",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/{{ inputs.mailbox | urlencode }}/mailFolders/inbox/messageRules",
            {"mailbox": param("string")},
            {"rules": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "object"}}},
            {"rules": "$.value"},
            doc="Attacker-created forwarding rules are the classic persistence in a "
                "business email compromise, and they outlive a password reset."),

        cmd("m365mail.delete_mailbox_rule", "M365: Delete Mailbox Rule", "DELETE",
            "https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/{{ inputs.mailbox | urlencode }}/mailFolders/inbox/messageRules/{{ inputs.rule_id | urlencode }}",
            {"mailbox": param("string"), "rule_id": param("string")},
            {"deleted": {"type": "boolean"}},
            risk="high", effect="mutating", success=[204]),
    ],
)

return [smtp, graph_mail]

Send Email is deliberately its own connector rather than a hidden platform
